historical_growth.growth_rate_source: underlying revenue growth (FY2025 +7%, H1 2026 +7%) less print run-off; equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable: shareholders' equity is shrunk by buybacks (GBP 1.5bn FY2025, GBP 2.25bn FY2026) and fell from 3,776 (FY2022) to 2,366 (FY2025) and 1,238 (H1 2026) while EPS compounded ~10%/yr. 5yr figures start from the COVID-depressed FY2020 base (Exhibitions revenue 362 vs 1,269 in FY2019) and overstate trend growth.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported OCF less capex, less IFRS share-based payment charge; interest income immaterial and the group is net debt, so not stripped). SBC is ~0.7% of revenue, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are near-identical. FY2023 OCF/SBC missing from the extracted text; FY2022 and FY2024 used as the adjacent anchors.

scenario_narratives.base: Underlying growth holds at ~7% near term (Risk +8%, Legal +10% on Lexis+ with Protege, STM stepping up, Exhibitions +6%), but reported GBP growth runs lower: FY2026 ~3.5% after ~2pt FX drag and ~2pt from disposals and print run-off (H1 2026 reported +2.7%). Reported growth of 6-6.5% through FY2029 as print shrinks to irrelevance, then fades to 3.5% by FY2035. Cost growth stays below revenue growth as guided: pre-SBC EBITDA margin 41.6% (FY2026) to 43.5%, i.e. adjusted operating margin ~35.5% to ~37%. AI is net neutral-to-positive: tools lift value per seat but capitalised development keeps capex above D&A throughout.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI-enabled analytics become a pricing and volume lever across all four segments: Legal sustains double-digit growth as agentic Protege moves from research into drafting workflows, Risk compounds on contributory fraud/identity data that general-purpose models cannot replicate, STM monetises Scopus AI/LeapSpace on top of strong submission growth. Reported growth 8% to FY2028 fading to 4%; AI also automates content operations, taking the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 45.5%. Terminal growth 3% (capped at 20x).
scenario_narratives.bear: The market's AI-disintermediation fear proves right at the edges: frontier-model legal assistants compress Lexis pricing in the mid-market, open access plus AI literature tools erode Elsevier subscription leverage and funders cut research budgets, privacy regulation restricts public-record data in Risk, and Exhibitions hits a travel/geopolitical down-cycle. Reported growth stalls at 2-3% (below inflation in real terms), and defending the franchise costs margin: pre-SBC EBITDA margin slides from 41.0% to 38.5% while development capex stays elevated. Terminal growth 2%, exit capped at 15x. The business remains strongly cash generative; this is a de-rating case, not a solvency case (net debt/EBITDA 2.3x).

valuation_philosophy.summary: RELX is a mature, high-margin compounder: ~7% underlying growth, ~35% adjusted operating margin, near-100% cash conversion, with surplus cash returned via buybacks funded partly by rising debt. The valuation rests on the durability of that growth-plus-margin algorithm against AI substitution, not on any turnaround. SBC is tiny (0.8% of revenue), so house and street values are close and the accounting-regime band is narrow. Value is terminal-heavy; the WACC/terminal-growth grid matters more than any single-year driver.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI substitution of legal research and scientific discovery tools compressing pricing power (bear axis)
Reported GBP growth diverging from underlying growth: ~60% of flows are USD/EUR and print/disposals remove ~2pt a year near term
Capitalised development spend rising faster than D&A (capex 6.0% vs 4.2% comparable amortisation in H1 2026) - if this is the permanent cost of AI products, FCF conversion runs below the base path
Leverage creeping up to fund buybacks: net debt 7.2bn to 8.7bn in six months; a re-rating of debt costs hits equity value directly
Data-privacy regulation of public-record and contributory data in Risk (37% of revenue)
Terminal value dependence: a 1pt WACC change moves value by roughly a fifth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE ADS, USD); 52-week range 27.57-43.36. FX from GBPUSD=X, parity-checked to REL.L.
data_sources.financials: RELX_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2025, H1 2016-H1 2026, GBP millions); RELX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt for net debt, share count, adjusted cash flow, capex split, D&A split, pension and guidance; RELX_Annual_FY2025.txt for FY2025 adjusted operating profit (3,342).

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 1,749.8m shares in issue net of treasury and Employee Benefit Trust shares (H1 2026 note, share table) plus 7.6m dilutive options/conditional shares (diluted weighted 1,794.1m less basic weighted 1,786.5m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The NYSE ADR is 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share, so no ratio adjustment.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-defined net debt at 30 June 2026: gross debt 8,906 (bank and bond borrowings 8,787 + lease liabilities 119) less cash 220, adjusted for hedging derivatives (+47 net asset), = 8,733. Debt minus cash alone is 8,686; the company figure is used. The GBP 500m of the 2026 buyback executed after 30 June is in neither the share count nor net debt (the two roughly offset at the current price).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 share-based remuneration charge GBP 63m (cash flow statement add-back). House basis uses the larger cash figure: GBP 76m of shares purchased by the Employee Benefit Trust in FY2025 to satisfy awards (net-debt reconciliation), since that is the cash the company actually spends to keep awards non-dilutive. RELX publishes no combined figure.
inputs.fx_note: GBP->USD 1.3212, Yahoo GBPUSD=X at 2026-11-13 close (epoch 1794703007). The bare RELX symbol is the NYSE ADS (1 ADS = 1 ordinary share), quoted in USD; statements and all flows are GBP. Parity check: REL.L 3,069.0 GBp = GBP 30.69 x 1.3212 = USD 40.55 against the ADS at inputs.current_price (0.1% tie), confirming rate, direction and the 1:1 ratio. refresh_price does not move fx_rate; re-date it on any update.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.0%, built in GBP: 10-year gilt ~4.5% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.8 (subscription/transactional information services, low cyclicality ex-Exhibitions) = cost of equity ~8.5%; pre-tax debt cost ~4.5% marginal (3.6% average on gross debt in H1 2026), ~3.5% after tax, at ~14% of capital = ~7.8%, rounded up to 8.0%. Roughly 55-60% of flows are USD, where the risk-free rate is similar, so no currency adjustment is needed. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt. Lease liabilities (119) are inside net debt; lease principal is NOT deducted as an operating cost. Renewal of right-of-use assets (~GBP 35-40m/yr, 0.4% of revenue) is charged through the capex line, matching the RoU depreciation (37) left inside D&A.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial: NCI profit share GBP 13m of 2,078m (0.6%) and NCI book equity GBP 17m. Flows are consolidated; NCI is deducted once, at book, in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year, three scenarios, probability-weighted (dcf-methods routing: non-US operating company, owner-fcf.md + adaptations). RELX is an information-analytics operating company whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; no bank/REIT/holdco features. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). EBITDA DEFINITION: RELX EBITDA = adjusted operating profit + depreciation and other amortisation, excluding amortisation of acquired intangibles (FY2025: 3,342 + 504 = 3,846, 40.1% of revenue; H1 2026 40.9%). That figure is AFTER the IFRS share-based charge, so the model's ebitda_margin_path is grossed up by the 0.8% SBC line to keep SBC explicit (FY2026 41.6% pre-SBC = ~40.8% company basis = ~35.4% adjusted operating margin). D&A path is depreciation and other amortisation only (5.3% FY2025), which is the tax-relevant base consistent with the 22.5-22.8% adjusted effective rate. CAPEX path = reported capex (5.5% FY2025, 6.0% H1 2026, mostly capitalised development) + pre-publication cost spend (~1.0%, capitalised in current assets, its amortisation sits in D&A) + RoU renewal (0.4%). CASH TAX 22.5% of EBIT: FY2025 cash tax paid 638 plus the ~65 interest shield = ~21% of adjusted operating profit; adjusted ETR 22.8% in H1 2026. WORKING CAPITAL: small positive capture (5% of revenue change) for prepaid subscriptions; adjusted cash conversion 98-100%. BASIS MISMATCH TO NOTE: last_fcf/reported_fcf are the levered CSV figure (OCF after ~GBP 260m net interest, less capex); the projections are unlevered, so year-1 projected FCF (~2.55bn) is higher than last_fcf by roughly the after-tax interest. BUYBACKS: funded repurchaser - GBP 1,500m in FY2025 and GBP 2,250m programme for 2026 (1,750 done in H1), far above the SBC charge; value-neutral in this model, flat count. FY2023 gaps in the Metrics CSV (OCF, SBC, D&A, equity) do not touch any driver: FY2025 and H1 2026 anchor everything. PRICE is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the thesis has a live, unresolved single axis - whether frontier AI models erode the pricing power of proprietary legal and scientific content - and the share price range over the past year shows the market treats it as a real probability; it is a de-rating risk, not a balance-sheet one (2.3x net debt/EBITDA, 98% cash conversion). Base 50%: guidance reaffirmed, +7% underlying growth with margin expansion is the run-rate of the last three years. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs sustained double-digit Legal growth, an STM step-up and further margin gains simultaneously, on top of a business already at ~35% operating margin.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
